pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. I could not run the tests: vitest is not installed here.
The item() renderer in src/index.js adds ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. Test 'AC-2' asserts the exact list text.

The code looks right, but the last commit (11ff87f) changed the normal-filter assertion in test 'AC-3' from toEqual(['First item']) to toBeDefined(). That can never fail. No other test checks that /?priority=normal lists exactly the normal items. The high and low filters are asserted properly, so the normal case is unproven.
Test 'AC-4' asserts the unfiltered list in id order after one item is set to low. The states test 'All priorities' also covers it.
Test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current one as <strong> and not a link.
src/index.js returns 400 when the priority param is present but not in the set, which includes an empty value. Test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks that no <li> appears.
Test 'AC-7' covers the no-match messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in all four views once the table is empty.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. Test 'AC-8' asserts it. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now allows a query string.

findings.what: Commit 11ff87f ('Follow-up edits', authored by a bot) loosened the normal-filter assertion from toEqual(['First item']) to toBeDefined(). A defined array always passes, so a broken normal filter would go unnoticed. The spec has no justification for loosening it. The 'One priority' state test only uses low, so nothing else covers the normal filter.
findings.fix: Restore expect(listed(...)).toEqual(['First item']), and ideally assert the full normal list (First item, plus any other normal items).

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'. That is false: the last commit loosened an AC-3 assertion to toBeDefined(). The PR also doesn't mention test/traffic.test.js's fake-app change beyond a brief note.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or disclose it. Correct the claim so it matches the diff.

findings.what: The README describes the ?priority filter but not the 400 on invalid values or the '— high' and '— low' labels. It also doesn't mention the filter links.
findings.fix: Add one line on the labels and the 400 response.

lenses.note: The spec is present. The code follows its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled.
The state table has a test for every row. AC-3 is unproven for the normal filter because the last commit loosened its assertion. The spec is unchanged after the go.
The loosened toBeDefined() assertion in test/priority.test.js is a high finding. I couldn't run the suite because vitest isn't installed.
The README is only partly updated.
The query is parameterised and the priority value is checked against a whitelist. Output is HTML-escaped. I found no defects in src/index.js.
No injection or secret issues. The bot-authored commit that weakens a test is covered under tests.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and there are no styles or components.
No browser or preview is available. The PR says there are no screenshots.
The claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is false. The title is under 72 characters.
